slides.text: Lecture thirty: skewed data and insights. Only fifteen point six percent of sessions end in a purchase.

The accuracy paradox: a model that always says no buy has eighty four point four percent accuracy, yet finds zero percent of buyers. With a skewed target, accuracy mostly measures the big class. Report recall, which is buyers found, F one, and R O C A U C, and always compare with the always-no baseline.

Sampling skewed data: take a small sample for a quick look. A random two percent sample, two hundred forty four rows, has eighteen percent buyers, versus the true fifteen point six. A stratified sample, taking the same fraction from each class, keeps the mix at fifteen point six. In pandas, group by Revenue then sample. The same idea: stratify equals y in train test split keeps fifteen point six percent buyers in both parts.

Three ways to handle skew in training. With no change, accuracy is point eight eight nine but recall only point four one six. With class weight balanced, recall is point seven eight five and F one point six two three, and no extra rows are needed. Under-sampling and over-sampling give similar recall of point seven eight five and point seven nine one. A small drop in accuracy, and recall nearly doubles. Do it only on training rows, because resampling before the split is the leak from lecture twenty nine.

Translating E D A into insights: observation, evidence, meaning, action. Valued pages drive buying: fifty six point three percent versus three point nine; intent shows on product pages; action: push visitors to product pages. November is the peak: twenty five point five percent, versus twenty point nine in October; holiday shopping; plan stock and ads for Q four. New visitors buy more: twenty four point nine versus fourteen point one; first visits are purposeful; offer a welcome deal. The test: a manager can act on it without reading your code.

The course review, the full pipeline. One: load and audit, duplicates and missing values. Two: E D A and hypotheses, refine then test. Three: features, from lectures twenty five and twenty six. Four: reduce, with P C A and V I F. Five: split, stratified eighty twenty. Six: pipeline plus cross-validation, fit on train only. Seven: test once, with recall, F one and A U C. Eight: insights, observation to evidence to meaning to action. The final model: C V R O C A U C of point nine zero, test recall point seven eight five, and the top signal is page values.

Key takeaways. Refine hypotheses and set the decision rule first. Split first, cross-validate on train, and test once. Leakage makes scores lie: point nine nine two versus an honest point six six five. For skewed data, judge by recall and F one, and resample train only. And an insight is observation, evidence, meaning, action. Thanks for watching.
